children: SYDNEY--Australian house prices in August extended their retreat and some are saying that the slide could eventually be among the worst on record.

The national home value index in August fell 0.9% from July, its fifth consecutive month lower, taking national home values 3.6% below the market peak recorded in March, according to Cotality, a property research group.
The downturn is becoming more widespread, with 93% of capital city suburbs recording a decline in house values through winter, the data showed.
Sydney leads the downturn with values down 1.4% in August and 7.1% below their peak, outpacing the city's 2022-2023 correction, Cotality said.
Quarterly sales tracked 15.5% lower than a year earlier, driving total advertised capital city listings 24% higher than a year ago as homes take longer to sell, it added.

The weakness in house prices nationally reflects the impact of three interest rates increases in the first half of the year, and major changes that affect the tax treatment of investment properties, announced by the federal government in May.

With the Reserve Bank of Australia now expected to raise interest rates further in coming months, perhaps as early as September, some economists are warning that the fall in house prices could accelerate.
Already there are a number of banks forecasting a peak-to-trough fall of more than 10%.
Cotality's five capital city index is now falling at an 11% annualized rate.

If that pace persists for 12 months, the slump will be the single worst correction in Australian home values in the 46 years of Cotality's data, Chris Joye, chief investment officer at Coolabah Capital.
"We already have the mother of all housing corrections on our hands," he added.
